in_text_mentions: estation of the disease, also had the most severe weakness in the extremities. Facial muscle weakness, diffuse fasciculations, absent tendon reflexes, and tongue atrophy were present in all subjects (Figure 1). Two patients had dysphagia and two had dysarthria. During examination, all patients had prominent hand tremor, and Patient 3 also presented with bilateral myotonia in the palms. Sensory assessment revealed glove and stocking-like sensory impairment as hyperesthesia for Patients 1 and 3 and hypoesthesia for Patient 5. Gynecomastia was observed in four out of five patients. panels.figure_caption: Atrophy and fasciculation of the tongue at the time of diagnosis of spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (SBMA).
in_text_mentions: At the age of 70 years, the patient suffered from dysphagia and dyspnea suddenly with the development of pyrexia within one month. An emergency tracheostomy was performed under local anesthesia after bilateral vocal cord paralysis was identified. Clinical examination revealed bulbar paralysis with atrophy and fasciculation of the patient's tongue (Figure 1).
